author: Spongiform
text:
Hello Les_Paul,

I love what you're doing with 'sweet FTRs'. I've been following a
similar line of thought for a while, what I call 'trading in the shadow
of the reaction to longer time-frame Supply or Demand'. I seem to keep
mangling this on the hard right edge: I think it's been down to a lack
of direction, and spending too much time in the detail rather than
stepping back and watching the big picture.

I'm a little late to the party, but I was particularly interested in an
FTR you pointed out (in post #317) in response to a question from Daft
trader 1 (in post #316). Fxyogi sort of picked up on it in post #340.

Here's your chart with the FTR in orange:

 Warning: Spoiler!

 [ Click to expand ]

 [ Click to hide ]

I'm sure it's a matter of what your rules say, but why did you pick that
 one over the lower one? I preferred the lower FTR but the reasoning is
discretionary. The difference between our choices is the difference
between viewing that spike down as an EG of one FTR or a reaction to the
 other (and thereby directional bias for potential trades). This is not
to say I made the better choice etc (and a visit to my journal shows my
preference for making the wrong choice as often as humanly possible ), but to understand the different philosophies and to learn... .

For comparison, here are some charts explaining how I thought both FTRs
(hindsight being 20 : 20 and all that, but I would have been attracted
to the one I've marked regardless).

 Warning: Spoiler!

 [ Click to expand ]

 [ Click to hide ]

H4 - first up, ancient history to give context to the PA of interest:

H4 - two views of the PA of interest. It shows your higher FTR and my
lower FTR. Mine occurs as a result of most recent PA, (to me) yours
seems to occur at an area from ancient history rather than a break above
 recent Supply (there are no orders from that time in the market, and
information quality degrades over time).

That higher FTR occurs at an interesting area. Market orders (Buy Stops
and breakout trader buys) are triggered right into that ancient Supply:
this would have been a great place for an FO if Pro Money wanted to move
 price down (having plundered liquidity to fill short orders) but
instead we see price grind higher (CP) immediately after. That CP
suggests hard work being done, and that suggests orders being filled.
This combined with my thoughts that this is a reaction to ancient
history (i.e. questionable) makes the upper FTR (which I thought of as
more of a DP, but I'm sure that's semantics) less utile than the lower
(in my opinion!). By comparison that lower one looks like it had an easy
 life:

H4 - for fun, a reminder that it's always advisable to look to the left for Stop placement on FTRs

W1 - and for more fun, stepping back would have shown a Flag in the
making, a pullback into Demand for a move higher (again, with the joy of
 20 : 20 hindsight):

Thanks in advance.

Spongy.
